In recent years, beekeeping has become popular on city rooftops. Many people assume that cities are bad places for bees because of pollution, but studies in several European capitals show that city bees often produce more honey than country bees. The reason is variety: parks, balconies and gardens offer flowers that bloom at different times of the year, while farmland may offer only one crop that flowers for a few weeks. However, experts warn that the trend has a downside. When too many hives are placed in one area, honeybees compete with wild bees for the same flowers, and wild species, which are already in decline, may suffer. For this reason, some cities now ask beekeepers to register their hives, and scientists recommend planting more wild flowers instead of simply adding more hives. A typical rooftop hive contains about 40,000 bees in summer.

They are healthier because of pollution.
They often make more honey than country bees.
They need fewer flowers than country bees.
